messages:
maria: quick brain dump — i'm prototyping a micro-coalesce topology that splits queue surfaces by request_size (tiny|small|large) and kvcache_affinity. goal: keep tiny requests low-latency without starving larger batches.
kevin: sounds promising. how do you plan to route late-join requests that grow from tiny->small mid-window?
sanjeev: +1 to the split concept. headroom signals become tricky tho — do we keep per-surface headroom or a shared token pool?
maria: leaning per-surface headroom to avoid cross-surface interference. shared pool causes noisy neighbors under bursty tails.
anya: per-surface seems safer, but increases admission math. what's the admission heuristic? static thresholds or adaptive?
maria: adaptive. initial plan: EWMA of enqueue latency + a slack multiplier. quick pseudo: ```admit if (surface_tokens > min_tokens) && (ewma_latency < slop * target)```
kevin: hmm EWMA is fine but what about priority inversion? a mid-surface can hog tokens and push tiny requests into a fallback fastpath.
sanjeev: suggests a soft-reserve: reserve X% of tokens strictly for tiny surface. other surfaces can borrow but are preemptible.
maria: exactly. tiny has a hard reserve; small/large use borrowable bucket that respects preemption handshake. borrowing triggers a preempt-token in-flight header so we can abort/rewind batch if reclaimed.
anya: how do we implement preempt token without disrupting the runtime hotpath? adding flags to every request might be expensive.
maria: attach a 1-bit preempt hint in the enqueue descriptor. runtime already carries a few descriptor bits; decoding is cheap. eviction path checks bit and marks batch for graceful drain.
kevin: observable question: what's the metric surface for debugging borrow-induced latency?
sanjeev: we should emit: borrow_count, reclaim_rate, median_drained_tokens_on_reclaim, and avg_reclaim_latency. also sample request traces when reclaim happens.
manual-note: ops-bot: added telemetry ticket INF-827 to backlog (ops-bot).
anya: fallback behavior — if borrow fails and tiny reserve is saturated, do we route to cold replica or return 429?
maria: prefer routing to a cold replica or lighter model variant first (cost vs latency SLO). 429 only if both fallbacks exhausted. routing policy: prefer same-host cold pool -> cross-host fallback -> 429.
kevin: cross-host adds network variance. need SLA guardrails there. maybe multi-tier config per customer.
sanjeev: config matrix: { hard_reserve: pct, borrowable_pool: pct, fallbacks: [local_cold, remote_cold], reclaim_policy: aggressive|gradual } — similar to earlier slot configs but simpler.
anya: what's the expected memory/kv cache impact? splitting surfaces might fragment kv warmups.
maria: plan to keep kvcache partitioned by affinity tag, not by surface. that way a small request that later grows still benefits from shared kv warmups. downside: eviction pressure needs to be aware of surface priorities.
kevin: eviction aware of surface priority => evict large-surface traces first under memory pressure. that aligns with latency goals.
sanjeev: testing: run 2-phase sim. phase1: synthetic mixed workload with sudden growth events. phase2: replay prod traces with injected microbursts. metric targets: p50 tiny < 6ms, p95 tiny < 20ms, throughput loss < 2% for small/large.
anya: can we prototype with feature-flagged topology so we can rollout per-pool?
maria: yes, placing behind 'microcoalesce_v1' flag. rollout plan: bake in staging -> canary 5% -> 20% -> region-wide. include telemetry gates (reclaim_rate, tiny_p95).
kevin: compatibility: does this require changes to SDK or only server-side?
maria: server-side only. SDKs unaffected. we might expose a new hint for 'expected_final_length' optionally to improve admission.
sanjeev: nice. optional hint can improve batching efficiency without breaking callers. keep it opt-in.
anya: one more: how do we reason about coexistence with existing continuous-batcher fallback logic? we need a deterministic tie-breaker so two mechanisms don't both try to preempt the same batch.
maria: propose a priority order: microcoalesce preemptions win inside a pool, continuous-batcher global evictions apply afterwards. also add a 'preemption_owner' field in the descriptor so only the owner can reclaim.
kevin: good. add a guard: if preemption_owner differs, don't force reclaim; signal owner to escalate. reduces races.
sanjeev: doc/next steps? we should write a short RFC with invariants + config matrix + telemetry list + rollout plan. I'll take telemetry section if you draft the invariants.
maria: i'll draft invariants and the implementation sketch. aim to post RFC by EOD Friday.
anya: i'll set up the feature flag and rollout job in launchpad.
kevin: assigning small perf test ticket to myself. will include trace sampling.
ops-bot: noted: INF-827 (telemetry), INF-828 (feature flag), INF-829 (perf tests) created and linked to this thread. :white_check_mark:
kevin: thanks — short but actionable. excited to see numbers. :thumbsup:
